summary: The 2D screening label is not_2d_applicable (input_gate_pass=false, scientific_gate_pass=false, independently_verified=false). Studio did NOT run: simulation status is skipped because a custom experiment needs 1-128 blocks and a power_w object, and the extraction supplied an empty floorplan and empty power_w. The scenario is the baseline 3-layer Cool-3D stack (cores at the bottom, two memory layers above, passive heat sink, no microfluidic cooling) running Splash2 fft, with steady-state HotSpot 7.0 results read from the Fig. 9 titles (PDF p.10): 395.52 K (core layer), 392.83 K (middle memory layer), 390.57 K (top memory layer). The experiment kind is custom_2d_steady, so there is no transient trace and no steady-or-transient comparison to a Studio output exists. This is not a bundled EV6/GCC adapted demonstration, and no pinned Ascend910 or ATPlace sizes/powers were used, so no illustrative input.flp or one-row input.ptrace was generated and no source commit or generated-placement assumption applies. The gate sets simulation_allowed=false and comparison_valid=false, so the final verdict is that no valid comparison exists. No numerical comparison is made, and exact replication is not claimed. The paper values are per-layer spatial maxima for a 3D stack from HotSpot 7.0 with a passive sink. Any Studio 2D result would involve a different location, aggregation, solver, boundary conditions and geometry. Qualitatively, the paper shows the core layer farthest from the sink as hottest, with layer maxima decreasing upward by about 2.7 K and 2.3 K. That is a 3D vertical-coupling effect that a single-layer 2D model cannot represent. These values are digitized from figure titles rather than a table, and no per-block data exist.

The scenario is a 3D stack of three dies (cores, memory banks, memory banks) with vertical heat coupling between layers. A generic 2D single-layer Studio thermal model cannot capture inter-layer coupling, the stack ordering effect or per-layer temperatures.

The cooling is a passive heat sink on a 3D stack, with the core layer at the bottom far from the heat sink. A Studio 2D package with its own cooling and boundary conditions does not reproduce this thermal path. Microfluidic cooling is used in later cases of the paper but not in this baseline.
The paper's power comes from a gem5, McPAT and CACTI-3DD pipeline over the fft workload. Per-block power values are not published, only heat maps, so no power rows can be taken from the paper.
The paper's solver is HotSpot 7.0 with a 3D layered floorplan and cooling configuration. Studio uses a different solver and material stack, so numerical agreement cannot be claimed.

The paper gives no block coordinates or dimensions in numeric form. The floorplan appears only as Fig. 9 heat-map images with unit labels such as C0_IALU and B_0, and the floorplan files are not in the packet.

The paper uses no optimizer or controller in the selected scenario, so there is nothing to mismatch there. Transient behavior is not studied, since the result is steady state, and reliability is not evaluated.
